q: Which is the most valid way to compare respiration rates of two invertebrate species with very different body masses?
options: Compare the total O2 volume used per tube, since body mass has little effect on respiration
Measure only the time taken for the fluid to start moving, regardless of the distance moved
Express rate as O2 used per gram per minute, with several animals and repeated trials
Use just one animal of each species, so that individual differences don't mix the results
explanation: Larger organisms use more O2 in total, so rates must be standardised per unit mass (e.g. mL O2 per gram per minute). Smaller animals usually have higher mass-specific rates. Using several individuals and repeats improves reliability; temperature, acclimatisation time, activity level and the amount of CO2 absorber must be kept constant.
